minutes.headline: Water commissioners backed the Zone 3 watershed bylaw for town meeting, if the water district is added to its approval list.
minutes.summary: Commissioners approved prior minutes, endorsed the planning board's Zone 3 water supply protection bylaw with one condition, and authorized the superintendent to hire the cheapest contractor to clean well number four. They discussed ARPA funding for PFAS work, lead service line outreach, the Hickory Hills pilot and the Mass Ave main job. They declined to approve a Stantec additional-hours request without more detail.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of September 6th (bid review meeting for the Mass Ave water main replacement)
Approve the Zone 3 water supply protection district bylaw to go to town meeting, provided the water department is added to the approval list
Have the superintendent hire the cheapest most efficient person to clean well number four

budget_items.what_was_said: Three items were approved: public education, a master plan, and a Keating well pilot study. The pilot study is the next priority after the public education piece.
A quote was in hand for the cleaning, with others pending. The superintendent was authorized to award to the cheapest, and the district has a well cleaning account.
A state grant covers the lead service line work, so residents are not charged. The district reviews and signs off bills, DEP pays, then the district writes the check.

budget_items.topic: Mass Ave main temporary water line
budget_items.what_was_said: Splitting the job would add temporary line costs, mentioned as a considerably higher price. The commissioners said it would likely still cost less if they got through winter without more breaks.
Stantec asked for payment for hours spent responding to MassDOT comments beyond its budget. The commissioners want a breakdown and any expected further amendments before approving.
An earlier review of bank fees and reconciliations was called a big success and credited to staff.

decisions.decision: Superintendent may award the well number four cleaning to the lowest of the quotes, comparing the hourly development time.
Commissioners will not approve the Stantec additional hours until a detailed breakdown is provided and reviewed.
Hickory Hills pilot: wait for DEP's response on the appeal before deciding on relocating outside the 100 foot buffer.
Superintendent to ask Fuss and O'Neill to prepare more lead service line outreach material, such as a Ledger ad with QR code and possibly a postcard.
No rush to sign the Mass Ave contracts; work is expected to start in spring.

topics.topic: ARPA funding, public education and PFAS master plan
Lead service line survey and public outreach

what_happened.line: Water commissioners voted to send the Zone 3 water supply protection bylaw to town meeting, on the condition that the water department is added to its approval list.
Commissioners voted to have the superintendent hire the cheapest, most efficient contractor to clean well number four.
Commissioners would not approve Stantec's request for payment of additional engineering hours until they receive a detailed breakdown; the item was tabled.
Commissioners told the superintendent to ask Fuss and O'Neill for more lead service line outreach material, such as a newspaper ad with a QR code.
Commissioners decided there is no rush to sign the Mass Ave contracts, with work expected to start in spring, and the Hickory Hills pilot waits on DEP's response to an appeal.

why_it_matters: The Zone 3 bylaw is headed to a town meeting vote, and the condition adds the water district to the list of bodies whose approval is needed for projects in the protected area around the town's water supply.
Well cleaning, the Mass Ave main and the engineering hours are paid from district funds, and the state grant for lead service line work means residents are not charged for it.
